cards.why: Harrowgate picked up and delivered it, its driver counted 12 cartons, and the delivery receipt notes 2 cartons crushed (Thursday 17 September 2026): good-order tender, damaged arrival and the amount make the prima facie case (Elmore & Stahl). 2 cartons of 4 Arden pendants at $172.50, $690 a carton, all broken: $1,380, full value, within 9 months of delivery. The receipt's notation is not itself a claim (49 CFR 370.3(c))

Concealed damage: the receipt is clean, but a clean receipt is evidence, not a bar. Thistlewood's packing record shows the shade sets packed to spec (double-wall, foam corners) and Harrowgate's driver signed for 10 cartons in apparent good order; Brightwell found the damage two days after delivery, reported it to Harrowgate within its 5 business days, and Harrowgate's own inspector found forklift-tine punctures at fork height. 3 Calla shade sets at $390: $1,170

Damage noted at delivery and confirmed by Harrowgate's inspector, but Rosa signed the released-value declaration for Harrowgate's released rate: liability is limited to $2.00 a pound (49 U.S.C. 14706(c)(1)(A); Rules Tariff HGF-100 item 780), and the crate weighed 85 lb. The claim is for $170, not the chandelier's $2,600 invoice price

The whole pallet, picked up Monday 12 January 2026, was never delivered, and Larkfield closed the trace 'unable to locate'. A trace is not a claim (370.3(c)), and Larkfield's terms give 9 months after the bill of lading date for a shipment never delivered: Monday 12 October 2026, three days away. 8 cartons at $407.50: $3,260, with Pellham's statement of non-receipt (370.7(c))

Larkfield's driver counted 8 cartons at pickup and delivered 7, the shortage noted on the receipt on Monday 28 September 2026, and Larkfield's own search came back not found: the brass finish carton, $940, at full value
